physical_parsing.volume_method: Ellipsoid over the body (elytra and pronotum, excluding mandibles): semi-axes 0.0175 x 0.010 x 0.0075 m, V = 4/3 pi abc. Mandibles add a small amount. Ellipsoid is a rough upper-bound estimate.
physical_parsing.shape_class: elongated ovoid (body) with long forward mandibles; overall a slender, dorsoventrally flattened prism

core.description: Torso core: head capsule anterior, prothorax, meso/metathorax and abdomen under the elytra. Leg roots attach at the thoracic sides; elytra and hind wings sit dorsally on the abdomen.

physical_parsing.size_source: Typical male Lucanus cervus body length 35-75 mm including mandibles (Wikipedia, Lucanus cervus; general reference knowledge, not fetched in this session). Modelled size 55 mm is a typical large male.

parts.name: head (with compound-eye bearing capsule)

penetration.overlap_region: anterior tip of pronotum collar, z 0.18-0.24 normalized

parts.notes: Head capsule carries mandibles, palps, antennae and eyes. Modelled as a block; hinge lets it tilt a little.

parts.name: pronotum (thoracic shield)

penetration.overlap_region: dorsal core under the pronotum, z 0.08-0.16

parts.notes: Broad, shiny, slightly convex shield over the prothorax. Mostly ornamental/protective; hides the head-thorax join.

parts.name: mandible (male, enlarged, branched)
parts.notes: Male mandibles are very long, antler-like, with a forward tooth. Used for male-male combat and grasping. Primary function is sexual display/combat, with feeding secondary. Length ~1/3 of total body length.

parts.name: maxillary palp
parts.notes: Small sensory-feeding palps near the mouth, tasting food. Very small; penetration is shallow.

parts.name: antenna (geniculate, 10-segment, short club)
parts.notes: Elbowed (geniculate) antenna: long scape, flexible flagellum ending in a short club. Chemo/mechanosensory.

parts.name: compound eye
parts.notes: Large lateral compound eyes, kidney shaped, fixed in the head capsule. Larger in males. Little or no eye movement.

parts.name: elytron (hardened forewing cover)

penetration.overlap_region: dorsal midline, scutellum, z -0.02 to 0.02, x 0 to 0.04

parts.notes: Hardened forewings that cover the hind wings and abdomen; they open upward to free the hind wings for flight. Protective; locomotion only when flying. Category kept as locomotion because they are part of flight mechanics.

parts.name: hind wing (membranous)

penetration.overlap_region: metathorax under elytra, x 0.00-0.06, z -0.14 to -0.06

parts.notes: Membranous flight wings folded under the elytra at rest. Gap: no library part for a folded beetle hind wing.

parts.name: foreleg (fore coxa, femur, tibia with teeth, 5-segment tarsus)
parts.notes: Tibia has toothed edge, used for digging and grasping. Males use foreleg mandibles to grip the female in mating. Locomotion is primary.

parts.name: midleg (5-segment tarsus)
parts.notes: Walking leg with a 5-segment tarsus and paired claws.

parts.name: hindleg (5-segment tarsus)

penetration.overlap_region: metathoracic side, x 0.20-0.28, y 0.26-0.34, z -0.28 to -0.16

parts.notes: Longest leg pair. Walking and grip on bark.

parts.name: foreleg (fore coxa, femur, tibia with teeth, 5-segment tarsus)

constraints.symmetry: bilateral about the sagittal (x=0) plane for all paired parts; head, pronotum on the midline
constraints.gait: hexapodal alternating tripod gait (fore + hind + opposite mid); tibial teeth for digging
other: Male mandibles are heavy; model a hinge with limited range so the mandibles do not clip the core.
Elytra hinge at the scutellum; open range limited to about 60 deg for flight.
Legs are pinned to the thorax, so the tarsi must stay in contact with the ground at y=0.

library_gaps.feature: folded membranous hind wing under elytra
library_gaps.why: library has wing_bat and wing_feather, neither a folded beetle hind wing

library_gaps.feature: geniculate (elbowed) segmented antenna with short club
library_gaps.why: library antenna is a generic single-piece shape
no part with a serrated edge

library_gaps.feature: paired elytra opening along a midline hinge
library_gaps.why: shell is a fixed plate, not a hinged cover
